exposure: co-infections of M. genitalium, N. gonorrhoeae, and/or C. trachomatis
cohort: The study included 416 maternal-newborn pairs from Papua New Guinea.
finding: M. genitalium and N. gonorrhoeae infections in pregnancy were associated with lower birthweight, and co-infections of M. genitalium, N. gonorrhoeae, and/or C. trachomatis had a larger negative impact on birthweight.
birth_weight: Birthweight was measured as an outcome; no specific inclusion/exclusion criteria for birthweight were mentioned.
